title: Gideon and the Hymn
premise: Folklorist Astrid Brightwater has spent three years in the village of Hollowmere recording a hymn no one will sing twice, dismissing the noises beneath the chapel as settling earth. When an excavation crew unearths a stone door sealed from the inside, Astrid discovers the hymn is half of a binding ritual the founders abandoned mid-verse, and their own fragmented memories are the missing verses. To reseal what stirs below, Astrid must let the found family they've built in Hollowmere sing them into the ritual — surrendering pieces of who they were to become the hymn's final voice. In the end, Astrid seals the door from within, remembered by the village only as a song that must never be sung twice.
about_author: Juniper Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obscure hymnals in coastal parish libraries before turning to fiction. They write horror about the things communities agree not to remember.

chapters.title: The Verse No One Finishes
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Recording elderly choirmaster Edith Vane, Astrid captures the hymn's first half before Edith stops mid-line, pale and refusing to continue. That night, knocking sounds beneath the chapel floor match the hymn's rhythm exactly. The emotional beat is unease: Astrid's rational explanations begin to crack as the village's silence starts to feel like protection rather than superstition.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Astrid and excavation foreman Dara Okafor. The crew breaks ground behind the chapel and unearths a stone door whose hinges are on the outside — it was barred from within. When Astrid touches it, they remember a childhood they never had, in a house that doesn't exist. The beat is dread deepening into complicity: the door recognizes Astrid, and something on the other side begins singing the hymn's second half.

chapters.title: What the Founders Started
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, with village voices intruding. In the parish archive, Astrid learns the founders wrote the hymn as a binding but died before teaching its final verse — a verse written in a person, not on paper. Villagers who once avoided Astrid now gather close, singing fragments that unlock more false memories. The beat is vertigo and tenderness entangled: Astrid realizes the family they've found here was assembled to complete them, and the thing below is nearly through.

chapters.title: The Last Voice
chapters.summary: Full village POV orbiting Astrid at the open door. As the seal fails, the villagers sing the completed hymn while Astrid, guided by memories both real and planted, speaks themselves into the final verse — each line erasing a piece of their identity. The door closes from the inside. The resolution is bittersweet: Hollowmere keeps its found family as a melody, and Astrid exists now only in a song the village refuses, out of love, to ever sing twice.
